label: Physics anchor: road-load estimate E_phys alone (+ simulation bands)
family_label: Physics model (generic road-load estimate, no learning)

compute.notes: no training: sim-train quantiles of log(y / E_phys) per architecture x duty (1.6 CPU s) + the two scale rungs (seconds)

feature_engineering: table: the input log E_phys (X[:, 90]); trace: E_phys recomputed from trace + spec + rl with EnergyNet's own features.phys_ints / e_phys (byte copy enet_features.py) = bake.e_phys_from_trace; strata of the bands: arch and class
rule: keep a rung if its sim val skill beats the incumbent by > 0.01 AND its dev D16 is not worse than the incumbent's by more than 0.01 (EnergyNet's model-rung rule, the harness's suggested rule)

rungs.change: E_phys with EnergyNet's dev-free defaults (PHYS_K, fitted by EnergyNet on simulations); bands = E_phys x sim-train quantiles of log(y / E_phys) per architecture x light/heavy duty
rungs.why: base; the point prediction equals the harness's E_phys reference row

rungs.change: x a per-powertrain scale fitted on SIMULATIONS (median log(y / E_phys) on the train bank, two tier draws: conv +0.198, hybrid +0.158, plug-in +0.089, BEV +0.069)
rungs.why: sim val skill 0.199 (+0.151) but dev D16 0.2521 vs 0.2278 (+0.024 > 0.01): the scale fixes city / cold trips (VED ICE 0.299 -> 0.153, EPA FTP 0.190 -> 0.107) and breaks highway, US06 and the ICCT truck (EPA HWY 0.093 -> 0.276, US06 0.078 -> 0.295, ICCT 0.865 -> 1.272)

rungs.change: x a per-powertrain scale fitted on DEV (scale calibration, not training: the median over the powertrain's dev sets of each set's median log(y / E_phys): conv +0.197, hybrid +0.163, plug-in +0.150, BEV -0.017)
rungs.why: sim val skill 0.203 but dev D16 0.2416 vs 0.2278 (+0.014 > 0.01) even IN-SAMPLE on the dev it was fitted on: one scale per powertrain cannot fix a city-vs-highway error
